claims.text: WxTaTiVCr tungsten-based high-entropy alloys can be fabricated by spark plasma sintering with in-situ TiC formation.
Spark plasma sintering produces a fine-grained WxTaTiVCr microstructure capable of accommodating TiC precipitates.
Tailored cooling rates and heat treatments can reliably produce matched variants with either a homogeneous coherent nanoscale TiC dispersion or minimal TiC precipitation.
TiC can be distributed within grains and along grain boundaries in W-based alloys.
The TiC precipitates in the proposed alloy are nanoscale and coherent.
Coherent nanoprecipitate interfaces in tungsten refractory high-entropy alloys facilitate dislocation transmission.
Coherent nanoprecipitate interfaces relieve stress concentrations that could cause premature crack initiation.
Coherent TiC precipitates facilitate dislocation nucleation.
Coherent TiC precipitates permit smooth dislocation transmission in WxTaTiVCr.
TiC precipitates act as crack-tip blunters.
The combined dislocation-mediation and crack-tip-blunting functions mitigate strain localization.
The engineered TiC dispersion increases plastic strain before failure at approximately 800 °C relative to a low-precipitate control.
The engineered TiC dispersion delays crack initiation at approximately 800 °C.
The engineered TiC dispersion slows crack propagation and improves fracture toughness at approximately 800 °C.
Enhanced dislocation-precipitate interactions modify the alloy's strain-hardening behavior.
A low-precipitate control has inferior high-temperature ductility because it has less effective dislocation mediation.
A low-precipitate control has inferior high-temperature toughness because it lacks crack-tip blunting.
The cited tungsten refractory high-entropy alloy retains a high yield strength at 800 °C.
The proposed controlled strain rates simulate fusion plasma-facing component service conditions.
The mechanism requires TiC precipitates to retain their size, distribution, and coherency during testing.

contradictions.description: The boundary declares substantial precipitate coarsening, dissolution, or loss of coherence to be outside the hypothesis's domain, while the falsification rule treats those same events as falsifying the hypothesis. An observation excluded by the stated boundary cannot also decisively falsify the bounded causal claim without further qualification.
